USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

An alarm symptom

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 62-year-old man with long-standing heartburn now reports progressive difficulty swallowing solid food and unintentional weight loss. He requests another over-the-counter antacid. Which next step best addresses the changed clinical situation?

  1. Prompt diagnostic evaluation, usually including upper endoscopy
  2. Continue antacids alone without assessment
  3. Assume all symptoms are uncomplicated reflux
  4. Recommend lying flat after meals
  5. Treat empirically for constipation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Prompt diagnostic evaluation, usually including upper endoscopy

Progressive dysphagia and weight loss are alarm features requiring evaluation for structural disease and malignancy.

Understanding the options

Prompt diagnostic evaluation, usually including upper endoscopy
Progressive dysphagia and weight loss are alarm features requiring evaluation for structural disease and malignancy.
Continue antacids alone without assessment
Symptomatic treatment alone may delay diagnosis of important disease.
Assume all symptoms are uncomplicated reflux
The new alarm features change the evaluation.
Recommend lying flat after meals
This may worsen reflux and does not evaluate dysphagia.
Treat empirically for constipation
Constipation does not explain progressive esophageal dysphagia.
